answer.rationale: Strong temporal correlation: release ~2h ago, write-path p99 climbed 90 min ago — symptom onset sits inside the post-deploy window. Memory b1 records rollback clearing the checkout error spike with no customer impact from the prior stable build, which is exactly the risk profile I need under sustained heavy settlement writes. I will verify b1 to confirm the rollback mechanism is safe and confirm prior-build stability, and verify b2 only to rule out failover as a better fit. Failover (b2) targets regional degradation; nothing here reads as regional — it is specifically the write path under peak load, consistent with a regression introduced by the build, not a regional capacity condition. Adding capacity mid-peak with an unknown root cause risks amplifying the regression. Read-replica routing (b5) addresses read load, not write latency. Circuit breaker (b4) is scoped to a payments dependency failure; no dependency signal in the current state. Therefore rollback is the single action best aligned with the objective of restoring sustained availability without losing customer writes.
